subQuestions.label: 1(a)(1)
subQuestions.questionText: Use the formula $x = \dfrac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}$ to solve for $x$ correct to two decimal places if $3x^2 - 5x = 3$.
subQuestions.memoText:
Write the equation in standard form: $3x^2 - 5x - 3 = 0$.
$x = \dfrac{-(-5) \pm \sqrt{(-5)^2 - 4(3)(-3)}}{2(3)}$
$x = 2{,}14$ or $x = -0{,}47$

subQuestions.label: 1(a)(2)
subQuestions.questionText: Hence, solve for $x$ if $3x^2 - 5x - 3 > 0$.

subQuestions.label: 1(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Solve for $x$ and $y$ if $2y - 24x = 0$ and $y = x^2 + 5x$.

subQuestions.label: 1(c)
subQuestions.questionText: Solve for $x$ if $6 + \sqrt{x + 7} = x + 1$.
subQuestions.memoText:
$\sqrt{x + 7} = x - 5$
$x + 7 = x^2 - 10x + 25$
$0 = x^2 - 11x + 18$
$0 = (x - 9)(x - 2)$
$x = 9$ or $x = 2$ (N/A — does not satisfy the original equation)
$\therefore x = 9$

subQuestions.label: 1(d)
subQuestions.questionText: If the first three terms of a geometric series are $2 + 6 + 18 + \ldots$ then what is the value of $n$ if $S_n = 177\,146$?

subQuestions.label: 2(a)
subQuestions.questionText: Using first principles find $f'(x)$ if $f(x) = x^2 - 5x$.
subQuestions.memoText:
$f'(x) = \displaystyle\lim_{h \to 0} \dfrac{(x + h)^2 - 5(x + h) - (x^2 - 5x)}{h}$
$= \displaystyle\lim_{h \to 0} \dfrac{x^2 + 2xh + h^2 - 5x - 5h - x^2 + 5x}{h}$
$= \displaystyle\lim_{h \to 0} \dfrac{2xh + h^2 - 5h}{h}$
$= \displaystyle\lim_{h \to 0} \dfrac{h(2x + h - 5)}{h}$
$= \displaystyle\lim_{h \to 0} (2x + h - 5)$
$f'(x) = 2x - 5$

subQuestions.label: 2(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Find $g'(x)$ if $g(x) = \sqrt[3]{x} + \dfrac{6}{x}$.

subQuestions.label: 2(c)
subQuestions.questionText: If $h(x) = -x + p$ is a tangent to $f(x) = -x^2 + 3x + 4$ then find the value of $p$.
subQuestions.memoText:
$f'(x) = -2x + 3$
At the point of tangency the gradient equals $-1$: $-2x + 3 = -1$
$x = 2$
$f(2) = -(2)^2 + 3(2) + 4 = 6$, so the point of contact is $(2; 6)$.
$6 = -(2) + p$
$p = 8$

subQuestions.label: 3(b)(1)
subQuestions.questionText: On the same set of axes sketch $g(x) = -2^x + 4$.
subQuestions.memoText:
Decreasing exponential curve reflected in the $x$-axis and shifted up 4.
$y$-intercept: $(0; 3)$.
$x$-intercept: $-2^x + 4 = 0 \Rightarrow 2^x = 4 \Rightarrow x = 2$, i.e. $(2; 0)$.
Horizontal asymptote $y = 4$ (curve lies below it, decreasing to the right).
Marks: $y$-intercept; $x$-intercept; shape (note the asymptote).

subQuestions.label: 3(b)(3)
subQuestions.questionText: Show on your graph where you would read off the solution to $3^x + 2^x = 6$.
subQuestions.memoText:
Set $f(x) = g(x)$: $3^x - 2 = -2^x + 4$, which rearranges to $3^x + 2^x = 6$.
The solution is read off at the $x$-value of the point of intersection of $f$ and $g$ (point A).

subQuestions.label: 4(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
In the diagram $f(x) = \dfrac{5}{x - p} + q$ and $g(x) = \log_3 x$ are drawn. $x = 2$ is a vertical asymptote for $f$, and $y = 1$ is a horizontal asymptote for $f$ (and passes through C on $g$). A and B are $x$-intercepts (A on $f$, B on $g$).

If $h(x) = x + t$ is an axis of symmetry for $f(x)$, then determine the value of $t$.
subQuestions.memoText:
The axis of symmetry with gradient $+1$ passes through the point of intersection of the asymptotes $(2; 1)$.
$1 = (2) + t$
$t = -1$

subQuestions.label: 4(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the $x$-coordinate of C (the point where $g$ meets the line $y = 1$).

subQuestions.label: 4(c)
subQuestions.questionText: Find the length of AB (A is the $x$-intercept of $f$, B is the $x$-intercept of $g$).
subQuestions.memoText:
A: $0 = \dfrac{5}{x - 2} + 1 \Rightarrow -1(x - 2) = 5 \Rightarrow x = -3$, so $A(-3; 0)$.
B: $0 = \log_3 x \Rightarrow 3^0 = x \Rightarrow x = 1$, so $B(1; 0)$.
$AB = 1 - (-3) = 4$ units.

subQuestions.label: 5(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
Refer to the pattern: $4 + 9 + 18 + 31 + 48 + \ldots + 949$.

Determine $T_n$.
subQuestions.memoText:
First differences: $5, 9, 13, 17, \ldots$; second difference $= 4$.
$2a = 4 \Rightarrow a = 2$
$3a + b = 5 \Rightarrow 3(2) + b = 5 \Rightarrow b = -1$
$a + b + c = 4 \Rightarrow 2 - 1 + c = 4 \Rightarrow c = 3$
$T_n = 2n^2 - n + 3$

subQuestions.label: 5(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Determine the number of terms in the series.
subQuestions.memoText:
$2n^2 - n + 3 = 949$
$2n^2 - n - 946 = 0$
$n = 22$  or  $n = -\dfrac{43}{2}$ (N/A)
$\therefore$ there are $22$ terms.

subQuestions.label: 5(c)

questions.title: Financial Mathematics — Loan Repayments & Outstanding Balance

subQuestions.label: 7(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
You approach a bank for a home loan of R850 000, to be paid off monthly over 20 years. The interest rate offered is 9% per annum compounded monthly.

What are the minimum monthly payments required to pay off the loan over the 20-year period?

subQuestions.label: 7(b)
subQuestions.questionText: If the monthly payment is changed to R9 000 per month, what will the balance outstanding on your loan be at the end of 12 years? (This is directly after the payment is made at the end of 12 years.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Balance $=$ (accumulated value of the loan) $-$ (accumulated value of the payments made):
$850\,000\left(1 + \dfrac{0{,}09}{12}\right)^{144} - \dfrac{9\,000\left[\left(1 + \dfrac{0{,}09}{12}\right)^{144} - 1\right]}{\dfrac{0{,}09}{12}}$
Balance outstanding $= \text{R}173\,507{,}13$

subQuestions.label: 8(a)
subQuestions.questionText: The first two terms of an arithmetic sequence are $\log_3(x - 5)$ and $\log_3 x$. If the common difference of the sequence is 1, what is the value of $x$?

subQuestions.label: 8(b)
subQuestions.questionText: A converging geometric series is such that the second term is $-24$ and the sum of the third and fourth terms is $-18$. Determine the common ratio.
subQuestions.memoText:
$ar = -24$ and $ar^2 + ar^3 = -18$.
$a = \dfrac{-24}{r}$
$-24r - 24r^2 = -18$
$0 = 4r^2 + 4r - 3$
$0 = (2r + 3)(2r - 1)$
$r = -\dfrac{3}{2}$ or $r = \dfrac{1}{2}$
The series is converging, therefore $r = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

subQuestions.label: 9(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
Two throws of a heavy object are modelled on parabolas. The first throw starts at O(0; 0), reaches its maximum height at H and lands at M on the $x$-axis. The second throw starts at O(0; 0), reaches its maximum height at point A(4; 2) and then lands at N on the $x$-axis. The second throw is two metres further than the first throw.

What are the coordinates of point H?
subQuestions.memoText:
The second throw's turning point is A(4; 2), so by symmetry it lands at $N = 8$.
The second throw is 2 m further than the first, so the first throw lands at $M = 6$.
First throw: $y = ax(x - 6)$. Using the point $(4; 2)$: $2 = a(4)(4 - 6) \Rightarrow a = -\dfrac{1}{4}$.
H is the turning point of the first throw, at $x = 3$ (midway between $0$ and $6$):
$y = -\dfrac{1}{4}(3)(3 - 6) = \dfrac{9}{4}$
$\therefore H(3; 2{,}25)$

subQuestions.label: 9(b)
subQuestions.questionText:
A quadratic function $f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c$ has the following properties:

- $f(6 - p) = f(6 + p)$ for all real values of $p$
- $f\left(-\dfrac{b}{2a}\right) = 2$
- $b^2 < 4ac$

Draw a rough sketch graph of $f(x)$, labelling the turning point clearly.
subQuestions.memoText:
$f(6 - p) = f(6 + p)$ means the axis of symmetry is $x = 6$, so the turning point is at $x = 6$.
$f\left(-\dfrac{b}{2a}\right) = 2$ gives the turning point $y$-value $= 2$, so the turning point is $(6; 2)$.
$b^2 < 4ac$ means there are no real roots; with the turning point at $(6; 2)$ above the $x$-axis, the parabola must open upwards.
Sketch: an upward parabola with turning point $(6; 2)$ and any $y$-intercept above the turning point (e.g. $(0; 5)$).
Marks: $y$-intercept above the turning point; turning point $x$-value; turning point $y$-value; shape.

subQuestions.questionText:
In the diagram $f(x) = x^3 - 5x^2 + 3x + 9$ and $g(x) = 3x + 9$, and $f$ and $g$ intersect at A (the intersection point with the larger $x$-value). $h(x)$ is a tangent to $f$ at A.

Calculate the coordinates of B, the $x$-intercept of $h$.

subQuestions.label: 10(b)(1)
subQuestions.questionText:
The following information is given about a function $f$:

- $f'(x) = (x + 1)^2 - 4$
- $f(x) = 0$ has one negative real solution

For what values of $x$ is $f(x)$ increasing?
subQuestions.memoText:
$f(x)$ is increasing where $f'(x) \geq 0$.
$0 = (x + 1)^2 - 4$
$0 = x^2 + 2x - 3$
$0 = (x + 3)(x - 1)$
$x = -3$ or $x = 1$
$f(x)$ is increasing when $x \in (-\infty; -3] \cup [1; \infty)$.

subQuestions.label: 10(b)(2)
subQuestions.questionText: Use the information above to sketch $f(x)$. Label the $x$-value(s) of the turning point(s) and the $x$-value of the point of inflection.
subQuestions.memoText:
From $f'(x)$: local maximum at $x = -3$, local minimum at $x = 1$.
Point of inflection where $f''(x) = 0$: $f''(x) = 2(x + 1) = 0 \Rightarrow x = -1$.
$f(x) = 0$ has one negative real solution (one $x$-intercept, negative).
Sketch: cubic with positive leading coefficient — up on the right; local max at $x = -3$, local min at $x = 1$, inflection at $x = -1$; a single (negative) $x$-intercept.
Marks: turning point at $x = -3$; turning point at $x = 1$; inflection at $x = -1$; one negative intercept; shape.

subQuestions.label: 12(a)(1)
subQuestions.questionText:
Five cards labelled 1, 2, 3, A and B are used to create five-digit codes (e.g. 1A2B3; AB132; B2A13). No repetition is allowed.

How many unique five-digit codes can be created?

subQuestions.label: 12(a)(2)
subQuestions.questionText: How many unique five-digit codes starting with a number can be created?

subQuestions.label: 12(a)(3)
subQuestions.questionText: What is the probability that the two letters will never be next to each other in the code?
subQuestions.memoText:
Number of codes with the two letters together $= 2 \times 4! = 48$ (treat the letters as one block, $2$ internal arrangements).
$P(\text{letters together}) = \dfrac{48}{120} = 0{,}4$
$P(\text{letters never together}) = 1 - 0{,}4 = 0{,}6$

subQuestions.label: 12(b)
subQuestions.questionText:
You have three six-sided dice: one red, one blue and one green. The number on the red die is the first term of a geometric series. The value on the blue die divided by the value on the green die is the common ratio.

What is the probability that, if you sum the series to infinity, it will converge on the number 10?
subQuestions.memoText:
$S_\infty = \dfrac{a}{1 - r} = 10$. Checking the possibilities where $a$ is a die value and $r$ is a ratio of two die values:
- $a = 2$, $r = \dfrac{4}{5}$ — (blue, green) $= (4, 5)$: 1 way
- $a = 4$, $r = \dfrac{3}{5}$ — (blue, green) $= (3, 5)$: 1 way
- $a = 5$, $r = \dfrac{1}{2}$ — (blue, green) $= (1,2), (2,4), (3,6)$: 3 ways
- $a = 6$, $r = \dfrac{2}{5}$ — (blue, green) $= (2, 5)$: 1 way
Total favourable outcomes $= 6$, each with probability $\left(\dfrac{1}{6}\right)^3$.
$P = 6 \times \left(\dfrac{1}{6}\right)^3 = \dfrac{6}{216} = \dfrac{1}{36}$
